content: 1. The United Nations General Assembly adopted Resolution A/RES/48/104 in 1993, which is a declaration focused on the elimination of violence against women. This document was published in New York by the United Nations. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) released a fact sheet in 2017 addressing violence against women, specifically intimate partner violence and sexual violence. This publication was produced in Geneva. 3. In 2013, the WHO published a report providing global and regional estimates of violence against women, including the prevalence and health effects of both intimate partner violence and non-partner violence. This report was also published in Geneva. 4. Stoltenborgh et al. conducted a meta-analysis in 2011 to provide a global perspective on the prevalence of child sexual abuse. Their findings were published in the journal Child Maltreatment. 5. The WHO published a report in 2012 titled Understanding and Addressing Violence Against Women: Sexual Violence, which provides insights into the issue of sexual violence. This report was published in Geneva. 6. UNICEF released a report in 2017 titled Attitudes and Social Norms on Violence, which examines societal attitudes toward violence. This report was published in New York. 7. Sumner et al. conducted a study on the prevalence of sexual violence against children and the utilization of social services in seven countries between 2007 and 2013. Their findings were published in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 2015. 8. Maniglio conducted a systematic review in 2009 to assess the health impacts of child sexual abuse. The findings were published in the journal Clinical Psychology Review. 9. Lundgren and Amin published a study in 2015 in the Journal of Adolescent Health that examined emerging evidence on the effectiveness of interventions addressing intimate partner violence and sexual violence among adolescents. 10. The WHO released a global plan of action in 2016 to guide health systems in addressing violence against women and girls. This document was published in Geneva. 11. Arango et al. conducted a systematic review in 2014 on interventions aimed at preventing or reducing violence against women and girls. This review was published by the World Bank Group in Washington, DC. 12. Namy et al. published a study in 2017 in Social Science & Medicine that explored a feminist understanding of intersecting violence against women and children within families. 13. The WHO published a report in 2016 titled INSPIRE: Seven Strategies for Ending Violence Against Children, which outlines evidence-based strategies to combat violence against children. This report was published in Geneva. 14. UNESCO released global guidance in 2016 on addressing school-related gender-based violence. This document was published in Paris. 15. The WHO published a programming tool in 2013 titled 16 Ideas for Addressing Violence Against Women in the Context of the HIV Epidemic. This document was published in Geneva. 16. The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine published an evidence overview in 2011 titled What Works to Prevent Partner Violence? This document was published in London. 17. The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights released Fact Sheet No. 23 in 1995, which addresses harmful traditional practices affecting the health of women and children. This document was published in Geneva. 18. The WHO published guidelines in 2016 on managing health complications resulting from female genital mutilation (FGM). This document was published in Geneva. 19. The WHO released a clinical handbook in 2018 on the care of girls and women living with FGM. This document was published in Geneva. 20. The United Nations adopted the Convention on the Rights of the Child on November 20, 1989. This document was published in New York. 21. UNICEF published data on female genital mutilation in 2018, providing insights into the prevalence and trends of this practice. This report was published in New York. 22. UNICEF released a report in 2016 titled Female Genital Mutilation/Cutting: A Global Concern, which highlights the global prevalence and implications of FGM. This document was published in New York. 23. The Population Reference Bureau published a report in 2017 titled Female Genital Mutilation/Cutting: Data and Trends, which provides statistical insights into the practice. This document was published in Washington, DC. 24. UNICEF released a report in 2014 titled Female Genital Mutilation: What Might the Future Hold? This document was published in New York. 25. UNICEF published a report in 2018 titled Child Marriage: Latest Trends and Future Prospects, which examines the prevalence and trends of child marriage. This document was published in New York. 26. UNICEF released data on child marriage in 2018, providing insights into its prevalence and trends. This report was published in New York. 27. Male and Wodon published a report in 2017 titled Child Marriage and Early Childbirth: Trend and Profile for 25 Countries. This document was published by the World Bank in Washington, DC. 28. UNICEF released a report in 2014 titled Ending Child Marriage: Progress and Prospects, which examines efforts to combat child marriage. This document was published in New York. 29. Koski, Clark, and Nandi conducted an analysis in 2017 on trends in child marriage across 31 countries in sub-Saharan Africa. Their findings were published in Population and Development Review. 30. Srinivasan et al. conducted a district-level study in 2015 on child marriage in India, examining its prevalence, trends, and patterns. This report was published by the International Center for Research on Women in Washington, DC. 31. Berg and Underland conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in 2013 on the obstetric consequences of FGM. Their findings were published in Obstetrics and Gynecology International. 32. The WHO Study Group on Female Genital Mutilation and Obstetric Outcome published a collaborative prospective study in 2006 in The Lancet, examining the obstetric outcomes of FGM across six African countries. 33. Wodon et al. published a global synthesis report in 2017 on the economic impacts of child marriage. This document was published by the World Bank Group in Washington, DC. 34. The United Nations Population Fund published a report in 2013 titled Motherhood in Childhood: Facing the Challenge of Adolescent Pregnancy. This document was published in New York. 35. Salam et al. conducted a systematic review in 2016 on potential interventions to improve adolescent sexual and reproductive health. Their findings were published in the Journal of Adolescent Health. 36. Kalamar, Lee-Rife, and Hindin conducted a systematic review in 2016 on interventions to prevent child marriage among young people in lowand middle-income countries. Their findings were published in the Journal of Adolescent Health. 37. Chae and Ngo published a report in 2017 titled The Global State of Evidence on Interventions to Prevent Child Marriage. This document was published by the Population Council in New York. 38. Shell-Duncan, Naik, and Feldman-Jacobs published a synthesis in 2016 on the state of knowledge regarding FGM. This document was published by the Population Council in New York. 39. Shell-Duncan, Njue, and Moore published a report in 2017 on the medicalization of FGM, analyzing available data. This document was published by the Population Council in New York. 40. Muteshi, Miller, and Belizán published a study in 2016 in Reproductive Health on the ongoing violence against women through FGM. 41. Arthur et al. published a study in 2018 in the Journal of Women, Politics & Policy on child marriage laws worldwide, examining minimum marriage ages, legal exceptions, and gender disparities. 42. The Southern African Development Community Parliamentary Forum published the Model Law on Eradicating Child Marriage and Protecting Children Already in Marriage in 2016. This document was published in Johannesburg. 43. The United Nations released a joint general recommendation in 2014 addressing harmful practices, combining insights from the Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination Against Women and the Committee on the Rights of the Child. This document was published in New York. 44. The WHO published a teacher’s guide in 2001 on integrating the prevention and management of FGM-related health complications into nursing and midwifery curricula. This document was published in Geneva. 45. The WHO released an interagency statement in 2008 on eliminating FGM. This document was published in Geneva. 46. The WHO published a global strategy in 2010 to stop healthcare providers from performing FGM. This document was published in Geneva. 47. The National Assembly of Zambia published the outcome document of a parliamentary seminar in 2018, which focused on ending child, early, and forced marriage. This document was published in Lusaka.
